title: Newton's law of universal gravitation
competency: Use F = Gm₁m₂/r², find g at a planet's surface and explain orbits with gravity as the centripetal force.

keywords.def: Every two masses attract with F = Gm₁m₂/r².
G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², the same everywhere in the Universe.
g = GM/R², about 9.8 m/s² at Earth's surface.
A force pulling a body toward the centre of its circle: F_c = mv²/r.

en.text: Every two masses attract each other with F = Gm₁m₂/r², where r is the distance between their centres and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg². The force is always attractive, acts along the line joining them, and is equal and opposite on the two bodies (Newton's third law). Doubling the distance makes the force four times smaller.

screens.title: Switch off the Sun
screens.ask: Imagine the Sun's gravity suddenly switched off. What would the planets do?
opts: Fly off in straight lines along the tangent
screens.after: With no force, Newton's first law says each planet keeps going straight at constant speed.

en.text: Your weight is the gravitational pull of the planet: mg = GMm/R². Cancelling m gives g = GM/R², about 9.8 m/s² on Earth. So g does not depend on your mass; it grows with the planet's mass and falls with the square of its radius.

en.text: A body moving in a circle needs a centripetal force F_c = mv²/r toward the centre. For planets this force is the Sun's gravity: GMₛ m/r² = mv²/r, so v² = GMₛ/r. With v = 2πr/T this gives T²/r³ = 4π²/(GMₛ), which is Kepler's third law with K ≈ 2.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ s²/m³.

screens.title: Why don't planets fall in?
screens.ask: The Sun pulls every planet. Why don't the planets fall into the Sun?
opts: They move sideways fast enough to keep curving round it
Gravity does not reach that far
screens.after: The pull bends the path into a circle; the large sideways speed keeps the planet from falling in.

screens.title: Centripetal force
paras: A force toward the centre of a circle is a centripetal force.
For planets, the Sun's gravity supplies it.
Earth's gravity does the same for the Moon and satellites.
Without it, a planet would go straight on.

screens.title: Kepler's third law from Newton
steps: Gravity = centripetal force: GMₛ m/r² = mv²/r.
Cancel m and one r: v² = GMₛ/r.
